title: Travel Protection Plans: Basis Q&A on the Uplift the Party Named Carries
content:
These questions are answered for the uplift the party named on a Travel Protection Plans certificate carries, when the premium the certificate now calls for is re-rated. Two things decide it: how many insured travellers the certificate names, and whether an age loading line stands on the certificate's premium record.

**Where the certificate names three or more insured travellers and its premium lines carry an age loading, what is the uplift the party named carries?**

It is 110 per cent of the premium.

**Where the certificate names two insured travellers and its premium lines carry an age loading, what is the uplift the party named carries?**

It is 105 per cent of the premium.

**Where neither of those holds, what is the uplift the party named carries?**

It is the whole of the premium and no more, 100 per cent of it.

## The three cases

| Insured travellers named | Age loading line on the certificate | Uplift the party named carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 or more | At least 1 stands | 110 per cent |
| Exactly 2 | At least 1 stands | 105 per cent |
| Any other combination | — | 100 per cent |

**Where the certificate names a single insured traveller, does the age loading matter?**

No. Neither of the first two cases is reached, because one requires 3 or more named travellers and the other exactly 2. The uplift is 100 per cent whatever the premium record carries.

**Where the certificate names four travellers but carries no age loading line, which case applies?**

The third, at 100 per cent. Both of the first two require an age loading line to stand on the certificate as well as the count of travellers.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** On a premium of 500.00 USD before the uplift: 550.00 USD at 110 per cent, 525.00 USD at 105 per cent, and 500.00 USD at 100 per cent.
